text:
Anya: Idea: introduce a tiny admission-control service (sidecar initially) in front of the runtime to accept or downgrade requested precisions (fp8/int8/4bit).

Mike: Quick clarifying Q — is this safety-only (prevent regressions) or also a cost/backpressure control?

Anya: Both. Objectives: 1) stop bad quality drops reaching customers, 2) throttle or reject aggressive low-bit lanes under memory/KV pressure, 3) make rollouts and canaries predictable.

Raj: How do we scope policies? per-model, per-customer, per-endpoint? Need a mapping to billing/quotas.

Anya: Policy stack: global -> model annotations -> customer overrides. Decision order: customer SLA -> model acceptability -> runtime health signals -> sampling guardrail. Outcome: final_precision OR explicit rejection.

Liz: Ops/billing worry: if we downgrade, how do we bill? We need a deterministic mapping.

Raj: We should emit a compact verdict proto for every decision: final_precision, reason_code, quality_risk_score, cost_estimate. Billing maps final_precision -> unit price.

Mike: Runtime contract idea: request headers like `x-precision-hint: fp8`, optional `x-quality-budget: 0.02`. Sidecar responds with `x-final-precision`, `x-admission-reason`, `x-admission-token`. Keep it tiny and deterministic.

Anya: Example policy DSL (ops-friendly):
```
policy: {
  default: { allowed: [fp16, int8], deny_on_high_load: true },
  model_overrides: {
    'redwood-research-1': { min_acceptability: 0.95, allowed: [fp16, int8, fp8] }
  },
  customer_profiles: {
    'acme-corp': { max_degradation: 0.005, must_preserve: ["safety", "ner"] }
  }
}
```

Liz: We need real-time quality signals. Proposal: shadow-sample ~1% of requests to a high-precision path and compute delta metrics (per-slice).

Mike: Shadowing is fine but beware KV/cache differences. Admission must correlate cache-hit and prefix-length when sampling quality deltas.

Anya: Agreed. Admission consults sliding-window stats for the model+customer slice; if degradation > threshold, auto-disable low-bit for that slice.

Raj: Rollouts: admin can force-allow or force-deny fp8 per-customer in console. Also need an emergency circuit-breaker toggle.

Mike: Runtime integration notes: sidecar should be sync and fast (<1ms goal). If sidecar is unreachable, runtime must choose a conservative fallback (FP16) rather than honoring the original aggressive hint.

Liz: Telemetry items: model, endpoint, customer_id, requested_precision, final_precision, admission_token, shadow_delta_pct, cache_hit, reason_code. Surface these in the Console per-route.

Anya: Security: customer overrides are admin-ACLed; policies stored in config-store with audit logs.

Raj: Ops want a canary flow: start with allowlist of internal customers, then staged ramp with observability gates. Add a billing doc for mapping precisions to unit costs.

Mike: Implementation plan: prototype as a sidecar so we can iterate policy rules without touching core runtime. Add a header shim that reads `/admission/verdict`. Keep the handshake minimal.

Anya: Important: verdicts must be idempotent for retries. Include request-id binding in the `x-admission-token` so retries observe the same final_precision.

Liz: Also surface a `quality_risk_score` (0..1) with the verdict so downstream APM can correlate incidents with admission decisions.

Mike: One more runtime concern: keep CPU overhead tiny. Admission should be mostly in-memory checks + occasional async calls to a stats backend for sliding-window reads.

Anya: Action items: 1) Anya to draft short RFC with policy DSL, API, and example rollout playbook (this week). 2) Mike to sketch sidecar shim + header API and open a small runtime PR (next week). 3) Raj to write billing mapping + canary runbook. 4) Liz to mock shadow-sample dashboard widgets and minimum alert rules.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flags/admission-sidecar -> canary toggles enabled in staging at 2026-03-24T18:00:00Z :rocket:

Mike: Caveat: ensure admission decisions are deterministic across retries and clones — tie verdict to request-id and short TTL.

Anya: We'll include TTL and request-id binding in the token. Thanks everyone — will follow up with RFC link.

Liz: :thumbsup: excited to see the dashboard.

Mike: ack, will review RFC/PRs when ready.
